prod_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me search for an available domain name for my startup using Namecheap. 

Before starting, ask me for:
1. My preferred business/brand name (or a few candidate names/keywords I want to use as the base for the domain).
2. Any preferred top-level domains (e.g., .com, .io, .co) in priority order, or tell me to assume .com first if I don't specify.
3. Confirmation that I have (or will use) a Namecheap account with configured credentials for any account-based lookups, if needed.

Once you have this information:
- Use Namecheap's domain availability search (via their dashboard or API) to check availability for the exact name(s) I gave you, across the preferred TLD(s).
- Also check a handful of sensible variations (e.g., adding "get", "try", "app", hyphens, or alternate TLDs) if my first-choice names are taken, so I have backup options.
- For each domain checked, record: the exact domain string, whether it's available, and the listed registration price if shown.
- Do not register or purchase anything at this stage — this step is search-only.

What done looks like: you have a clear list of at least 5-10 checked domain options with availability status and pricing, including my original preferred name(s) and reasonable alternates if those are taken.

Report back to me with:
- A simple table or list: domain name | available (yes/no) | price (if shown).
- A short recommendation of the top 2-3 available options based on brand fit and price.
- Confirm you did not register or purchase any domain — that decision remains a human step, and I will tell you which one to proceed with next.

prod_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me register a custom domain through Namecheap as the first step of setting up my startup's domain (DNS, SSL, and hosting will be configured in later steps). Before starting, ask me for: (1) the exact domain name(s) I want to check and register, in priority order (e.g., mystartup.com, mystartup.io); (2) whether I want WHOIS privacy protection enabled; (3) the registrant contact details to use (name, organization, email, phone, address) if not already saved in my Namecheap account; and (4) confirmation that I have a Namecheap account with configured credentials and a valid payment method on file.

Once I provide this, use my configured credentials to log into Namecheap and check availability for each domain in my priority order. For each available domain, note the registration price, renewal price, and any add-ons Namecheap offers (privacy protection, auto-renew). Prepare a clear summary showing: the recommended domain choice, its price, the registration term (e.g., 1 year), whether privacy protection is included, and the contact details that will be used for registration. Add the domain to the cart and fill in the registrant information and any settings I specified, but do NOT complete the purchase or click any final 'buy'/'checkout' button.

Because this involves a real financial transaction, you must stop for human sign-off before finalizing the registration. Present me with the prepared cart summary, total cost, and any settings you applied, and wait for my explicit approval before completing the purchase.

Report back with: the domain(s) checked and their availability status, the recommended domain with pricing and settings prepared in the cart, and a clear statement that the purchase is pending my sign-off.

prod_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me transfer DNS management for my custom domain to {{vendor}}, the edge-platform service I've chosen for this arena. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my domain name, and (2) confirmation that I have (or will set up) a {{vendor}} account using my configured credentials.

Please do the following preparation work, but do NOT apply any changes yet:
1. Sign in to {{vendor}} using my configured credentials and check whether a zone already exists for my domain.
2. If no zone exists, prepare (but do not finalize) the steps to add my domain as a new zone in {{vendor}}, including reviewing the DNS records {{vendor}} detects/imports from my current provider so I can confirm nothing important is missing.
3. Note the nameserver values {{vendor}} will assign once the zone is created, so I can update them at my domain registrar afterward.
4. Compile a clear checklist summarizing: the domain, the zone status, the imported/expected DNS records, and the nameserver change required at the registrar.

Because this step requires my explicit approval before any change is applied, do not create the zone, change nameservers, or modify any DNS records — just prepare everything and present the checklist. Then stop for human sign-off.

Once I approve and you (or I) make the change, note that zone activation is asynchronous — {{vendor}} needs the registrar nameservers updated and then verifies the zone status, which can take time. In that case, describe how you would poll/check the zone's active status later rather than assuming immediate completion.

Report back with: the zone status found, the checklist of records and nameservers, and confirmation that you are stopping for my sign-off before any change is applied.

prod_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure DNS records for my custom domain using {{vendor}}, an edge-platform service that offers free auto-renewing TLS certificates (including wildcards) and lets me attach custom domains to deployed services. 

First, ask me for: (1) my domain name, (2) the target hosting endpoint or service the domain should point to (e.g., a deployment hostname or IP), and (3) confirmation that my {{vendor}} account and zone for this domain are already set up with your configured credentials. 

Once you have these, use the available {{vendor}} MCP tools: first use the search tool to locate the correct DNS records endpoint in the {{vendor}} API for creating records in my zone, then prepare (but do not yet execute) the exact record(s) needed — typically an A/AAAA or CNAME record pointing to my hosting target, plus any additional records required for domain verification if applicable. Present me with a clear draft showing: record type, name, target value, TTL, and proxy/SSL-relevant settings, along with the exact API call you intend to execute. 

Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve changes before they are applied, do not call the execute tool yet. Summarize the proposed DNS changes in a checklist and then stop for human sign-off. Once I confirm approval in a follow-up message, you may proceed to execute the create-record call via the {{vendor}} API. 

Report back with: the finalized record details prepared for approval, confirmation that no changes were applied without my sign-off, and (after approval) the result of the executed API call including any errors or confirmation of successful record creation.

prod_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me add a custom domain to my project hosted on {{vendor}}. Please prepare everything needed but do not apply any changes until I explicitly approve, since this step requires my sign-off before execution.

First, ask me for: (1) the exact custom domain (and any subdomains, e.g. www) I want to attach, and (2) the name of the {{vendor}} project this domain should be linked to. If you have configured credentials for {{vendor}}, use them to look up the project and confirm it exists.

Then do the following preparation:
1. Check whether the domain is already registered under my {{vendor}} account or organization, and note its current status.
2. Determine what DNS records (e.g. A record, CNAME, or nameserver changes) {{vendor}} will require to point the domain at this project, and draft the exact record values needed.
3. Draft the specific action you would take to attach the domain to the project via the {{vendor}} dashboard or API, described in plain language (no raw endpoint calls).
4. Note any SSL/certificate provisioning that {{vendor}} will handle automatically once the domain is verified, and any manual verification step required.
5. Summarize all of this into a clear checklist: domain name, target project, required DNS records, and expected verification/SSL outcome.

Once this checklist is ready, present it to me for review and stop for human sign-off — do not add the domain, modify DNS, or trigger any {{vendor}} changes yourself. Report back with the full checklist, any discrepancies found (e.g. domain already attached elsewhere), and a clear statement that you are awaiting my explicit approval before proceeding.

prod_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me verify that SSL/TLS is correctly configured for my custom domain on {{vendor}}, the edge platform I use for hosting/DNS. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my domain name(s), including any subdomains or wildcard patterns I want covered, and (2) confirmation that I have access to my {{vendor}} account using my configured credentials.

Please do the following:
1. Log into {{vendor}}'s dashboard (or use its API/CLI if that's how I normally manage it) and locate the SSL/TLS certificate settings for my domain.
2. Confirm a certificate has been issued and is active for the apex domain and all required subdomains/wildcards, and that it was issued via {{vendor}}'s free automatic certificate service rather than manually uploaded.
3. Verify the certificate's validity dates and confirm auto-renewal is enabled so it will renew before expiry without manual action.
4. Check that the domain's DNS/hosting records correctly point to {{vendor}}, since misconfigured pointing can prevent certificate issuance or cause validation failures.
5. Test the live site over HTTPS (e.g., by fetching the URL) to confirm the browser/connection shows a valid, trusted certificate chain with no warnings, and that HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS if that's expected.
6. If any subdomain or wildcard is missing coverage, or the certificate is expired/pending/invalid, note the specific issue and what setting needs to change.

When done, report back: the domain(s) checked, certificate status (active/pending/expired), issuing method, expiry date, auto-renewal status, whether all subdomains/wildcards are covered, and results of the live HTTPS test. Flag any problems found and what you were unable to verify or fix, so I know what still needs attention.
